authority.representation: Normal mapped scalar-only registry: 64-byte header, 48-byte descriptors; all uint64 cells aligned; no managed references in registry or payload
authority.identity: Control-mapping-derived engine-lifetime process identity plus positive never-reused descriptor index; wrapper identity is irrelevant; raw addresses remain trusted runtime metadata
authority.creation: Native 64-bit seq-cst CAS lock serializes quota reservation and publication. Read count/quota from native header, map maximum once, write immutable descriptor, then publish count and release lock. No managed allocation/callback while lock held; actual raw host leaves satisfy this contract.
authority.budget: Payload quota charges page-rounded maximum, at least one page even for zero-length blocks; registry mapping separately bounded by maxBlocks. Invalid page policy is rejected before mapping.
authority.rollback: Failed maps publish nothing or consume no count/quota. Owned misaligned mappings are unmapped before publication; rollback failure is fatal rather than silently losing ownership.
authority.growth: Authoritative per-block 64-bit seq-cst length CAS loop, including equality. A failed CAS observes newer length; if target is now smaller, return invalid-length. Reserve once, no copying, zero-filled untouched new bytes.
authority.payload: 1/2/4-byte integer operations remain whole-width; Word64 uses lo/hi and caller output scratch. Metadata conversion to Number is only for explicitly bounded safe-integer metadata.
authority.scratch: Each operation owns a fresh metadata scratch; grow/create reuse only their own scratch inside retry loops. Caller Word64 output is separate and preserved on validation failure.
authority.lifetime: Successful mappings retained through engine/process lifetime; no finalizer/refcount/destroy claims, no registerExternalMemory grant, no premature unmap
